summary: Independent GRAVEYARD red-team pass challenged all 12 active-batch theses against concentration, policy, dilution/capital intensity, cyclicality, execution, substitution and common-shock risk. No thesis is falsified outright. The largest hidden fragilities remain CRDO/ARM customer concentration, NVDA/AMD/ASML export sensitivity, RKLB/VRT backlog quality, MU peak-cycle normalization and batch-wide dependence on the same AI-capex regime.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Large backlog can conceal cancellation rights, margin mix and long conversion duration while Neutron adds schedule/capital risk.
contradictions: Demand validation is real but does not prove Neutron economics.
unknowns: Backlog cancellation composition and exact Neutron cash need.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Repeated schedule slips, cancellations or negative unit economics persist despite scale.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Latest quarter still shows extreme end-customer concentration; rapid growth can reverse nonlinearly if one hyperscaler changes architecture or procurement.
contradictions: Excellent margins/cash coexist with cliff-like customer dependence.
unknowns: Program duration, pricing protection and customer insourcing risk.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Top-customer loss causes abrupt growth/margin compression.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Scorpio ramp concentrates execution around a product transition and a narrow AI-platform customer set.
contradictions: Profitability lowers solvency risk but not design-win concentration.
unknowns: True end-customer concentration and cancellation visibility.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Scorpio misses ramp guidance or a major platform design is delayed/lost.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Customer concentration and export controls create simultaneous revenue and substitution risk; restricted markets can accelerate domestic alternatives.
contradictions: Exceptional demand coexists with policy-created TAM loss.
unknowns: Long-run custom-accelerator wallet share and future restriction breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: CSP internal silicon gains material share while NVIDIA margins/software lock-in weaken.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Data-center momentum does not guarantee durable accelerator economics against NVIDIA/custom silicon; export licensing adds inventory and TAM uncertainty.
contradictions: Growth is strong but repeat-scale breadth remains under-proven.
unknowns: Instinct customer concentration and normalized accelerator margin.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: MI-series remains pilot-concentrated or software gaps limit repeat deployments.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Custom-AI exposure can be concentrated in a few powerful customers; VMware leverage/integration adds a separate execution path.
contradictions: Very strong FCF buffers balance-sheet risk but not customer bargaining power.
unknowns: AI customer shares and exact deleveraging path.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Major custom programs migrate away or VMware integration underdelivers materially.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Commercial diversification does not remove Taiwan as a physical single point of failure; overseas redundancy may structurally raise cost.
contradictions: Technology leadership coexists with geopolitical concentration.
unknowns: Normalized overseas-fab margin drag and customer resilience premium.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Competitor process/yield lead or Taiwan disruption materially impairs advanced-node output.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: EUV scarcity is exposed to export policy, customer capex cyclicality and High-NA ROI risk.
contradictions: Backlog/gross margin indicate pricing power but policy is outside company control.
unknowns: Current China mix and High-NA utilization economics.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Order deferrals broaden while High-NA economics disappoint and restrictions expand.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top-five customer concentration, Arm China dependence and SoftBank/control relationships reduce apparent asset-light resilience; RISC-V remains a credible substitution vector.
contradictions: Royalty economics are excellent yet monetization/control remain concentrated.
unknowns: Incremental server/AI royalty economics and long-run RISC-V share.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Major licensees shift material new workloads away from Arm without offsetting royalty growth.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Historic HBM/memory profitability can invite supply response; low-looking valuation on peak earnings can conceal mean reversion.
contradictions: Longer agreements improve visibility but memory remains supply-responsive.
unknowns: Contract floors and competitor HBM4 capacity/yields.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: HBM share/yield loss or rapid supply expansion compresses ASP/margins.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: High margins can mask cloud-titan concentration and architecture risk from proprietary fabrics/internal networking.
contradictions: Cash-rich balance sheet reduces financing risk, not strategic concentration.
unknowns: Current top-customer share and 1.6T buyer breadth.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Cloud AI spend slows or proprietary fabrics take material scale-out share.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Very high book-to-bill/backlog can contain reservation, cancellation and execution risk; power/interconnection constraints can delay customer projects independently of Vertiv demand.
contradictions: Order breadth supports real demand while conversion quality remains under-normalized.
unknowns: Backlog aging/cancellation terms and customer concentration.
perCompanyCoverage.falsifier: Cancellations rise or backlog conversion slows materially for multiple quarters.

materialFindings.finding: CRDO and ARM retain the sharpest directly evidenced concentration vulnerabilities in the batch.
The active batch is economically concentrated in one AI-infrastructure spending regime, so a hyperscaler capex reset is a common shock across many nominally separate tickers.
Backlog/order strength at RKLB and VRT is not equivalent to backlog quality; cancellation, aging and schedule economics remain material hidden variables.

contradictions: Record operating growth and strong balance sheets do not remove concentration/policy/common-shock fragility.
Backlog visibility can coexist with weak cancellation/schedule quality.
unknowns: Comparable end-customer concentration is not yet normalized across the entire batch.
Backlog cancellation rights/aging are inconsistently disclosed.
Current diluted-share normalization remains incomplete for several names.

peerRequests.request: Prioritize CRDO/ARM customer concentration and RKLB/VRT backlog-quality normalization; preserve dilution/share-count blockers.
Stress one shared AI-capex downshift across semiconductor/interconnect/power-cooling names and identify which economics survive.

accuracyDebates.reason: Ticker count materially overstates thesis diversification in this batch.
Avoids promoting raw backlog/book-to-bill into durable demand without cancellation/aging evidence.
